#2043. Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is "the right character" for the Red Devils but he has "a lot to prove"

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 22:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:06

Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.

A nice easy start. United have only won one Premier League game this season, so there are no easy games at the moment.

It is a quick turnaround for Pochettino. He had the second USA game against Haiti, finishing at midnight UK time on Tuesday, then flew straight to England and into Carrington to begin work, and was back in again today, Thursday, to prepare.

The preparations are far from ideal with players coming back from international duty, but they are what they are. I think what will be very interesting going forward is the shape Pochettino settles on. I still think it will be a 4-2-3-1 for the majority.

We know Pochettino likes high pressing and fast attacking transitions. There are suggestions he likes Marcus Rashford a lot, though perhaps more the Rashford of a few years ago than the one who has been injured and is potentially coming back in.

He likes his full-backs to attack. The counter-pressing. He likes his attacking midfielders to be creative, so expect Bruno Fernandes to be given fewer defensive duties and more of a free role in that number 10 position.

Pochettino spoke about mentality and togetherness, the culture, and he will want his team aligned. There are no suggestions the players threw Carrick under the bus.

Ultimately it was a mixture of Carrick not being tactically good enough and the players not responding in the end to the management style. The change had to happen.

He speaks on Friday afternoon and will give a team news update at that point. Suggestions are that Harry Maguire had a slight injury in the Villa game but should be fine. Luke Shaw may or may not be fit. Marcus Rashford may or may not be fit. There will be no Sesko. There will be no Baleba. Lisandro Martinez is back from his suspension.

Patrick Dorgu is back too. He did not play for Denmark over the break but came off the bench to great effect against Villa last time out.

Suddenly there are a lot more options in the defensive areas of the pitch, which has been the major problem for Man United this season.

The midfield is going to be interesting for this game. Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo started against Villa. Andrey Santos is an option in that area of the field as well.

Mason Mount has played there, but I am not convinced by Mount in central midfield. Baleba being out is a big one, because I feel he could be a key player under Pochettino.

There are suggestions he will be out for a shorter period than initially thought after picking up that muscular injury against Roma in the Champions League.

Can Dorgu get himself back in the team? He could be a big player for them going forward. But for now, the key thing is getting the team together and working out how they are going to play.

There is no rest for the wicked either. They go to Portugal next week for the Sporting Lisbon game in the Champions League, then welcome Brentford, then Newcastle and Coventry, then back in Champions League action against Leipzig.

This period is incredibly busy. The fact that Pochettino was appointed at the end of last week and then had to wait through that second USA game is not ideal, but we have had ideal preparations before and it has still gone wrong anyway.

I do like the Pochettino appointment. He has got a lot to prove. He seems like the right character, and you can tell he really wanted this job.

It is the job he has been linked with numerous times without it ever coming off. Now feels like the right time, and hopefully United can get something against Liverpool.

United's recent record against Liverpool is good. Three games unbeaten, winning both Premier League games last season, including that 2-1 win at Anfield with that late Harry Maguire header.

United are down in 18th in the Premier League: one win, five draws, four defeats. Fourteen goals scored is not awful. Nineteen goals conceded is awful.

Gary Neville said recently that the back four that finished against Villa would get you relegated, and it is difficult to argue against that, but it should be strengthened for this match.

One Premier League win all season is diabolical. Ultimately it is why Carrick lost his job. But the recent performance against Villa, getting two late goals and avoiding defeat, was a major positive.

Going forward, the story is Pochettino, but it is also the players. Where is the professional pride? Can there be a bit more solidity at the back and an end to the defensive errors?

Senne Lammens has had a good start to his career but questions are now being asked. There are a few shots going in around him that he really should be doing better with, and what is happening in front of him is not helping in that regard.

I would like to see a settled team in the Premier League. Changes have to happen for European games, but get a settled team, get the system playing, get Fernandes in his best position, and get the wingers sorted, whether that is Rashford. Amad Diallo has not scored in almost a year now, so he may have to come out of the team.

I think you are keeping Mbeumo through the middle. Cunha has been decent of late. He has got the players there. Looking forward to this one and we will see what Pochettino can come up with.

#2038. Capello pays tribute to Baresi and is ‘waiting for results’ after Cardinale’s bold claims

Fabio Capello recalled what Franco Baresi meant to him as a player and captain, while commenting on Gerry Cardinale’s bold declarations too.

Few players mean more to a club – if any – than Baresi meant to Milan. The centre-back reinvented the role and became a symbol of one of the most dominant eras in the history of the sport, as well as an icon in the eyes of the fans who adored him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Capello was lucky enough to coach the No.6 and he spoke about Baresi’s greatness on Andrea Longoni’s YouTube channel ‘Milan Hello’. His words were relayed by MilanNews, and the emotion was clear in his voice.

“He was important for what he conveyed to the other players when they came to play for Milan. I’m talking about champions, important players, foreigners, of all qualities. They saw in him the man who conveyed the history of Milan,” he said.

“Franco didn’t talk much in the dressing room, but when he did, he was listened to because you could feel his words came from the heart, you could feel they were something important for everyone.”

Last night, Capello was interviewed by Sky and he commented on Cardinale’s words, who has been making some quite bold pledges about Milan’s future in recent weeks.

“He’s promising a lot with his words, I read everything he says. Now I’m waiting for him, I’m waiting for the results. I want to see if he’ll do what he’s saying, if he has a plan and a real idea of ​​where he wants to get to.

“Berlusconi had also promised great things, but then he surrounded himself with people who knew about football. Besides the players, you also need to create a staff that follows you and understands your ideas.

“Now I don’t know if this staff has already been chosen, he keeps talking about new sporting directors, about new people who will join Milan. Let’s see what he can do. The promises are great, we’ll see what the results will be.”

#2037. Mansfield Town vs MK Dons - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 22:55, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00

MK Dons will be targeting a seventh consecutive win in all competitions when they head to the One Call Stadium for Saturday’s League One encounter against Mansfield Town.

The visitors head into the weekend in ninth spot, while the Stags are two points worse off in 12th place in the League One table.

Mansfield occupy a midtable position after recording five wins, four draws and four defeats in 13 league games.

The Stags enjoyed a run of three wins in four league outings before they fell to a 2-0 home defeat against Notts County at the end of October.

Mansfield then played out a goalless draw against Wigan Athletic before they returned to winning ways with a 3-0 victory against sixth-tier Macclesfield in the FA Cup, setting up a second-round clash against fellow League Two side Colchester United.

Nigel Clough's charges netted three more goals in their EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, but they were left with nothing to show for their efforts after shipping four times in the final half-hour of a 5-3 defeat, ensuring they finished the group stage without a point to their name.

Mansfield will now turn their focus back to League One action, and they should fancy their chances of picking up at least a point, having lost just one of their six home games in the third tier this term (W3, D2).

Having failed to win their last three head-to-head home matches, Mansfield are aiming to beat MK Dons at the One Call Stadium for the first time since August 2006.

MK Dons, meanwhile, are in red-hot form after winning each of their last six competitive games, including four successive victories in League One.

After beating Stevenage, Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in the third tier, MK Dons kicked off their FA Cup campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Swindon Town.

Paul Warne's charges backed up their FA Cup success with another 2-1 win in their EFL Trophy clash with Bromley, sending them through to the Round of 32 as Group H winners.

Sam Nombe then netted a brace in an emphatic 6-2 victory in last Saturday's home clash against Burton Albion, making it the third consecutive home league game in which MK Dons have scored four or more goals.

In stark contrast to their free-scoring home form, MK Dons have netted just seven goals across their six road trips in the third, although they only required one goal to claim their first away league win of the season against Stevenage last month.

Saturday's visitors can take confidence from the fact they have won two of their previous three away games against Mansfield, including a 2-1 success on their last visit to the One Call Stadium in March 2024.

Mansfield are expected to be without Liam Thompson, Lucas Akins and David McGoldrick due to injury.

Bailey Cargill, George Abbott and Louis Reed are making progress in their respective recoveries, but it remains to be seen whether they will be ready for Saturday’s fixture.

Mansfield will also assess the fitness of Deji Oshilaja and Frazer Blake-Tracey, the latter of whom picked up a hamstring issue in the defeat to Chesterfield.

As for the visitors, Warne remains without the services of Ryan Barnett, Kane Wilson and Rushian Hepburn-Murphy.

Aaron Collins is back from international duty after making his Wales debut as a substitute in Tuesday’s 3-2 defeat to Portugal in the UEFA Nations League.

As League One’s top scorer with 13 goals, Collins is expected to lead the line alongside Nombe, which means Callum Paterson will likely have to settle for a place on the bench despite scoring in the last two competitive games.

Dennis; Ekpiteta, Sanders, Goode; Silvera, Gilbey, Wintle, Crowley, Campbell; Paterson, Nombe

MK Dons will be full of confidence after winning six games on the bounce, and we think they will continue their impressive run of form against a Mansfield side that has won just one of their last four competitive outings.

#2033. Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55

Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.

Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.

Meanwhile, new Palace boss Thomas Frank takes charge for the first time with less than a week of training under his belt, tasked with ending a four-match losing run and lifting the London club above their West Midlands hosts.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Coventry and Crystal Palace.

Over 118 years have passed since Coventry City and Crystal Palace first locked horns - an FA Cup tie in January 1908 that ended in a 4-2 victory for the Eagles - and there have now been 114 competitive meetings between the two clubs across all competitions.

There is very little to separate the sides historically, with the Sky Blues holding the narrowest of edges on 41 victories, while Palace are hot on their heels with 38 wins and another 35 encounters have ended all square.

More than 14 years have elapsed since their most recent clash in March 2012, when the two teams shared the spoils in a 1-1 Championship draw in the West Midlands several months after Palace had edged a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park.

Coventry's last triumphs in this fixture came during the 2010-11 campaign, when they recorded back-to-back 2-1 home wins in the FA Cup and Championship in January and February 2011 to avenge a 2-0 defeat in South London earlier that season.

Prior to that double, Palace had enjoyed a dominant spell over the Sky Blues, putting together a 10-match unbeaten run across all competitions between September 2005 and November 2009 that included seven wins and three draws.

That sequence featured five consecutive victories for the Londoners - highlighted by emphatic 4-1 and 4-2 away triumphs - before Coventry finally ended their hoodoo with a gritty 1-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 2010.

This weekend's showdown marks their first Premier League meeting in over 28 years, with the clubs last crossing paths in the top flight in February 1998 when Coventry ran out 3-0 winners in South London.

Across their six previous Premier League encounters, the Sky Blues hold the upper hand with two victories to Palace's one alongside three draws, and remarkably neither side has ever won a home game in the competition.

Palace's lone Premier League success in this fixture was a 4-1 away demolition in November 1994, whereas Coventry claimed 2-0 and 3-0 victories on the road in February 1995 and February 1998 respectively.

Before the Premier League era, Coventry were a formidable force against Palace in the old First Division, going unbeaten in their first 14 top-flight meetings between 1969 and 1990 - winning 10 and drawing four - before the Eagles finally broke their duck with a 2-1 win in December 1990.

Knockout meetings have been rare, with Palace winning three of their four cup ties - including 3-0 and 1-0 League Cup successes in 2002 and 2005 - while Coventry's most emphatic results in the fixture date back to their Division Three (South) days in the 1930s, when they dished out 8-0 and 8-1 home thrashings in 1932 and 1935.

Mar 06, 2012: Coventry 1-1 Crystal Palace (Championship)

Aug 16, 2011: Crystal Palace 2-1 Coventry (Championship)

Feb 12, 2011: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace (Championship)

Jan 08, 2011: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace (FA Cup)

#2027. Bradford City vs Doncaster Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:09

Bradford City and Doncaster Rovers will square off on Saturday in a Yorkshire derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The hosts sit a point outside of the playoff places following a defeat last time out while their visitors have dropped into the bottom four due to consecutive losses.

Bradford City head into their first League One game of November at the weekend following an international break with the hopes of returning to winning ways and moving back into the top six.

After winning promotion from League Two and losing in the League One playoffs in the last two seasons, the Bantams picked up where they left off in early 2026-27, winning five of their first seven outings before Graham Alexander departed for Preston North End.

They then turned to Michael Duff and have struggled to continue their hot start since, winning one, drawing four and losing one of their last six league matches with the only victory coming against Stevenage in mid-October.

That did form part of a run of four straight clean sheets for the Bantams, who top the division with nine and have conceded a league-low tally of eight goals, but that came to an end in their last league outing against fellow promotion-chasers and Yorkshire rivals Huddersfield Town, who dished out a 3-0 beating at Mbanq Valley Parade.

Now, at least, on the back of a pair of confidence-boosting cup wins before their break, beating Marine 7-0 in the FA Cup and York City 4-0 in the EFL Trophy, Bradford City now sit eighth, but just two points off fourth spot, and will hope to retake a top-six spot and kickstart another hot streak in League One.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip across Yorkshire in search of a return to winning ways of their own in their battle at the other end of League One.

Doncaster Rovers also won promotion from League Two in 2024-25 and finished 14th last time around on their return to the second tier but now find themselves 21st with just 12 points on the board from 13 games.

That is in no small part down to a poor away record, having lost five of seven games on the road, collected just four points and conceded 16 goals in those.

Two heavy away defeats have come consecutively for Grant McCann's side since a home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, as they lost 3-1 at Luton Town and 6-1 in their last third-tier match away at MK Dons at the end of October.

Having also since played two cup games, beating Rochdale in the EFL Trophy and losing 3-0 away at non-league Kidderminster Harriers in the FA Cup, Doncaster Rovers now head into a tough trip aiming to kickstart an upturn in form in League One and climb out of the bottom four.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):

Bradford City remain without wide men Josh Neufville and Tyreik Wright, while attacker Bobby Pointon also missed their last outing through injury.

Corey O'Keeffe will continue in a wing-back role in Neufville's absence, while Antoni Sarcevic will start in midfield having served a suspension in the FA Cup for a red card received in their last league game.

George Lapslie, Adam Phillips and Nick Powell will all compete for starts in attack after Jake Beesley led the line with support from Kayden Jackson and Will Swan in the 3-0 defeat to Huddersfield.

Doncaster Rovers continue to contend with several injury issues, as James Collins, Francis Okoronkwo, Matty Pearson, James Husband and Tommy O'Reilly should all remain sidelined.

McCann made some rotations in their two cup games and should make changes from the team that lost 6-1 to MK Dons in their last league outing, with the likes of Robbie Gotts and Will Keane pushing to start after being reduced to substitute appearances.

Hakeeb Adelakun will also challenge for a start on the wing and may join Isaac Hutchinson and Jordan Thomas in support of a lone striker unless captain and key man Owen Bailey returns to an advanced midfield role.

Bradford City have certainly not been at their best in League One since Michael Duff's arrival, but still boasting the league's standout defensive record, and having rebuilt confidence with a pair of dominant cup wins, we back them to come out on top at home to a struggling Doncaster team.

#2026. League, Trophy, Senior Cup – in-form Eastbourne Borough just have to keep rolling

As winter approaches, Borough's schedule in the coming weeks is piling up nicely - or even alarmingly. Isthmian Premier fixtures including rearranged dates - the Sussex Senior Cup, and an early December trip to Oxford City in the third round of the FA Trophy.

How do clubs, players and managers shuffle the diary, juggle the commitments, and stay both physically fit and mentally focused? Not that anyone wants any weather disruption as winter approaches - but it's rather like being the adult in the middle of your children's snowball fight, and the cold wet missiles are coming at you from every angle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"We just keep going!" said boss Steve King. "Is that seventeen out of nineteen? I lose count! We get them back in the dressing room and we just count the bodies, see who we have available match by match - and we go again!

"The trip to Enfield Town (on Saturday) is massive. There are players who possibly could come back, after Tuesday night (the victory over Littlehampton Town). We'll take a look at it."

Tired bodies? Aches and strains? "The lads just want to keep going! There's a massive togetherness, a determination. You can have all the talent in the world, but application is the crucial thing! It's game by game, and we'll just keep going!"

The Sports head for North London tomorrow (Saturday) to take on Isthmian Premier pacesetters Enfield Town. A six-pointer? The Towners - relegated with Borough last season - are a tough proposition, especially at their distinctive home stadium - a favourite of groundhoppers, with its ocean-liner main stand, grass pitch and open, running-track arena.

And then, as sure as Tuesday follows Saturday, Borough will welcome Aveley for the next midweek encounter. The Essex club snatched victory away from King's team in the first match of the season, equalising in stoppage time - but Borough have been on an upward trajectory ever since, and King will be looking for a very minimum of four points from the coming pair of fixtures.

A sweeping Tuesday night victory over Littlehampton Town has seen Borough into the last eight of the Sussex Transport Senior Cup - where intriguingly, Eastbourne United have also secured their place with a notable victory at Bognor Regis Town.

What price a local derby next up? The quarter-final draw also includes most of the Sussex big-hitters: Lewes, Horsham and Chichester City among them. Two ties remain - Wick versus Worthing, and Hastings United's trip to Whitehawk - before Borough learn their next opponents.

After Tuesday's 6-1 win over Littlehampton, Steve King's verdict was measured. "It was alright! In the first half we had chances but we weren't clinical. We weren't happy with the goal that we conceded - showing the opponent inside rather than the outside. But the second half was much more fitting of us and we scored some cracking goals.

"Solid at the back, and we came good in the end. I was really pleased for Owen Hargreaves, on the scoresheet with a brilliant goal. He works so hard week by week, and it was just reward. Owen is a great example of a player who is learning and improving all the time. He's in the team alongside quality players and players with experience, and that's bringing the best out of him.

"Tyano (Wilson) is a similar example, great natural ability, learning all the time - when to pass, when to cross, when to fill holes - the decision-making.

"Now after two cup competitions, it's back to the league at Enfield. Second versus third, but it's still only three points like any other game, and it won't define the season. Enfield are a very good side, and they're up there on merit. But so are we!"

#2025. Feyenoord vs SBV Excelsior - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:13

Feyenoord host SBV Excelsior at Stadion Feijenoord (De Kuip) in Rotterdam in round 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday.

The Pride of South sit second in the Eredivisie table on 25 points, one behind PSV after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen on November 8, while Excelsior are 15th on 11 points, one clear of the relegation play-off place after five straight league defeats.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side arrive without a win in five matches in all competitions, having lost 1-0 at Real Betis on October 21, drawn 1-1 with PSV and Fortuna Sittard, lost 3-0 at home to Inter Milan on November 3 and lost 5-3 at Heerenveen.

Heerenveen was Feyenoord's first league defeat of the season, and it came after they led 2-0 through Anis Hadj Moussa and a Nacho Ferri penalty, only for substitute Ringo Meerveld to score a hat-trick.

Their attack has not been the problem, as 36 league goals in 12 games trail only PSV's 40, and a 5-0 home win over Utrecht on September 20 featured two goals from Hadj Moussa plus strikes from Ferri, Luciano Valente and Gaoussou Diarra.

The damage is coming at the other end, where Feyenoord have conceded seven goals in their last three league games after allowing 10 in the first nine, and they have let in at least one in each of their last five matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Tjark Ernst, signed from Hertha BSC for €5m in the summer, received sarcastic applause from home supporters after a routine catch against Inter, and Opta figures published by NOS rate only two Eredivisie goalkeepers worse than him at keeping out shots, although Van Bronckhorst continues to select him.

Captain Valente said after the Heerenveen defeat that things clearly had to change, while Van Bronckhorst has said that opponents have adapted to the way Feyenoord play.

Ruben den Uil's side won 4-0 at Cambuur in their opening game to go top of the Eredivisie for the first time in 47 years, and they had 10 points from five games after a draw at NEC on September 8.

Since then Excelsior have taken one point from a possible 21, a run of seven games that includes a 2-2 draw at Ajax on September 19 despite being outshot 33-8, a 1-5 home loss to Groningen and a 4-0 defeat at Heerenveen on October 16.

In their last five league games, Excelsior have conceded 20 goals and scored once, a stretch that includes a 9-0 defeat by Twente on November 1, the heaviest in the club's league history, in which Nesto Groen was sent off after five minutes for a challenge on Robin Propper.

Go Ahead Eagles then won 1-0 at Excelsior on November 7 through Soren Tengstedt, in a game Den Uil described as a typical 0-0, which left the Kralingers without a goal in four league games and on 16 for the season, four of which came in the opening win at Cambuur.

Aymen Sliti, who has three league goals, and defender Jan Plug are both on loan from Feyenoord, and Sliti has said he will not celebrate if he scores at De Kuip.

Feyenoord have eased the restrictions on visiting supporters for the derby, who will not be required to use organised transport to De Kuip.

Hadj Moussa is a major doubt after a sprained ankle on international duty with Algeria following the game against Togo, and Feyenoord-watcher Martijn Krabbendam said on Voetbal International's podcast that reaching the derby will be difficult, with the club aiming to have him ready for the Klassieker against Ajax on November 29, although Kicker reported that he left the Algeria camp after a dispute with the coach rather than through injury.

Jeremiah St. Juste is still out with a shin problem and Van Bronckhorst hopes to have him back before the winter break, while Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen are not expected until after it and Tijme Wessels is recovering from knee surgery.

Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie are available again after injuries, Gijs Smal has returned to group training and Jakub Moder, who has played one minute this season, is also being eased back, although neither is certain for Saturday and no Feyenoord player is suspended.

For the visitors, Groen misses the derby serving the last game of a three-match ban, with one match suspended, for the red card against Twente, which leaves Mario Dominguez or David Garden to lead the line.

Sliti hurt his hand in the Netherlands Under-21s' 3-2 defeat by Denmark on November 17 and fears a bruised or broken thumb, but he has said he expects to play on Saturday, with former Feyenoord winger Alireza Jahanbakhsh the alternative on the flank.

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Van Persie, Ferri, Valente

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Yegoian, Hartjes; Naujoks, Thorsteinsson, Sliti; Dominguez

Feyenoord have won each of their last six meetings with Excelsior, scoring at least twice every time, including 2-1 wins on August 16, 2025 and March 15, 2026, and Excelsior have not won at De Kuip since 1980.

That record matters because this Excelsior side has conceded 20 goals in five league games, has lost Groen up front and faces an attack that has scored 36 times in 12 league games.

Feyenoord's own defence, which has conceded in five straight matches, and the possible absence of Hadj Moussa leave a small opening, but Excelsior have failed to score in each of their last four league games, so we expect Van Bronckhorst's side to win without needing to rely on one player.

On that note, Wood said the club’s ‘pathway’ was beginning to bear fruit, and he praised the younger teams’ coaches for developing some highly promising talent. Some are knocking on the first-team squad’s door – others are being loaned out to step five clubs.

United’s women’s team are having a tough run in the London and SE League Division 1. Wood said it was a transistional campaign and hard work was going into building the women’s set-up.

#2021. Groningen vs Heerenveen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:31

FC Groningen host SC Heerenveen in the Eredivisie at Euroborg on Saturday, November 21 in the first Derby of the North of the 2026-27 season.

Sixth-placed Heerenveen arrive on 21 points on the Eredivisie table after four consecutive league wins, while ninth-placed Groningen have taken one point from their last four games and will be without their head coach, goalkeeper and first-choice right-back.

Groningen have collected one point from their last four Eredivisie matches, a run that began with a 2-5 home defeat to Ajax on October 18 and included a 2-2 draw at NEC Nijmegen.

Those four games have cost 14 goals, and the 2-3 home loss to Sparta Rotterdam on November 1 came after Jacob Ondrejka scored after 17 seconds, before a miscommunication between Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer handed Andrej Kostic the winner in the 85th minute.

The latest setback came at AZ on November 8, where De Trots van het Noorden led 3-1 after 54 minutes, lost 4-3 to a Mexx Meerdink penalty in the 91st minute and finished with nine men after Vaessen collected a second yellow card for protesting the penalty and Hateboer was sent off in the 10th minute of stoppage time for a deliberate handball.

Euroborg has offered little protection this season, with Groningen winning two, drawing one and losing three of their six home league games, and a 2-0 home defeat to Dick Lukkien’s former club FC Emmen ended their KNVB Cup run in the first round on October 29.

The recent derby record still favours the hosts, who won 2-1 at Euroborg on August 16, 2025 through a stoppage-time Brynjolfur Darri Willumsson goal and 2-0 at Abe Lenstra Stadion on January 18, 2026, when captain Thijmen Blokzijl scored the second.

The off-field story is Lukkien, who had a hip replacement last week and said the derby arrived “just too early” for his recovery, so assistant Casper Goedkoop will coach from the touchline.

Heerenveen have won four consecutive league games since a 2-0 defeat at PSV Eindhoven, beating Excelsior 4-0, ADO Den Haag 3-2, NEC Nijmegen 1-0 and Feyenoord 5-3.

Those wins have brought 13 goals and five conceded, including two from Jacob Trenskow at ADO on October 24, and have lifted De Superfriezen to 21 points from 12 games with a goal difference of +8.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the unbeaten league record of the Eredivisie leaders, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a late Ringo Meerveld hat-trick.

Meerveld came on at half time for Maxence Rivera and scored in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes, with Trenskow providing the pass for the first of them.

Away from Abe Lenstra Stadion, Robin Veldman’s side have won two, drawn two and lost one of their five league trips, but they have not won in Groningen since a 2-0 victory on March 19, 2023.

Veldman said after the Feyenoord game that his players wanted to extend the run, and a win would take them further clear of seventh-placed Fortuna Sittard, who sit on 20 points.

Vaessen and Hateboer are both suspended after their red cards at AZ, so Lovro Stubljar, who has been on the bench in recent league games, is expected to start in goal and Wouter Prins should move in at right-back.

Malcolm Jeng remains out with an Achilles tendon injury and goalkeeper Rijk Janse is also sidelined, while Travis Hernes and Ryan Metu are doubtful after several weeks out.

Heerenveen have no reported injuries or suspensions, so Veldman has a full squad to choose from.

Meerveld is expected to push Rivera for a start on the left of the attacking three after his hat-trick off the bench.

Stubljar; Prins, Blokzijl, Rente, Csinger; De Jonge, Clement; Schreuders, Van Bergen, Ondrejka; Willumsson

#2014. Barnsley FC v Sheffield Wednesday: Davis Keillor-Dunn the danger now Owls have worked out his numbers game

Davis Keillor-Dunn's sale – or rather the way the Reds responded to it – is symptomatic of why home fans are so grumpy with their club, with protests against the management planned before and during the televised derby game.

In the short-term, the bigger worry is now he is in blue-and-white stripes, the Owls are belatedly starting to work out how to best use him.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Wearsider is a versatile forward, which is not always as helpful as it sounds.

At Barnsley he scored 16 goals as a "false nine" last season before joining Wrexham on February’s deadline day. Swallowed up in their squad, he failed to score for the Dragons, and even though David McGoldrick stepped up to find the net in his absence, the failure to spend the fee on a replacement summed up why some home fans plan to chant "Enough is enough" four minutes into Friday’s derby.

After bringing the 29-year-old back to South Yorkshire on loan, Henrik Pedersen used Keillor-Dunn from the right, the left and in the hole before asking him to lead the line, the job his successor Dave Challinor has earmarked for now.

Three goals in as many games, six in his last nine, suggests the Owls are starting to find the right formula.

"With Ali (Al-Hamadi) being out, he's probably the closest," says Challinor when asked if his squad lacks a genuine 'No 9'. "Harry (Gray) I think will develop into a nine, but as an 18-year-old playing in League One, the physical part of that is always going to be tough for him.

"Davo's probably a nine-and-a-half. He can play as a nine but also likes to link the play."

For those not au fait with football's trendy numbers game, a No 9 is a traditional centre-forward who leads the line, either as a targetman or playing off the shoulder of the last defender. A 'ten' plays in the hole behind, and a "false nine" or "nine-and-a-half" flits between the two, as Harry Kane does for England.

And although Challinor spoke after Saturday's 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle about the need for Keillor-Dunn to get into positions to score proper striker's goals, as he did that day, it does not mean shackling him at the top of the pitch.

"I'm okay with him dropping off," he insists. "The important thing is that when the ball is in certain areas, he gets in the right areas. If the ball is in a wide area, he's a box finisher.

"I've shown him all his goals over the last three years and 90 per cent, 95 per cent, are within the width of the posts in the 18-yard box. If the ball is in a wide area, we want him in the box. That's where he'll finish.

"There's nothing to say that outside of that we don't want him working and running channels.

"As long as the majority of his stuff is in central areas and we're getting the ball to him, if he wants to impact the game in different areas, then great, but only on the odd occasion.

"I'll go back to the Oldham game (Challinor's first as manager, in the FA Cup first round) in the first half. He spent far too much time almost as a left wing-back, which is not playing to his strengths.

"(The message was) go and get close to the goal, he gets a goal, he gets the same on Saturday, another couple of opportunities within that.

"We will give them freedom, but freedom within the structure."

Quite what that structure will be is a challenge for Daniel Stendel's Barnsley players. It is hard for the coach to tell them exactly how the Owls will play when, three games in, Challinor is still working it out.

"We prepare the team for the next opponent every time," says Stendel. "But I think two different things (about Wednesday).

"A new manager has come in, but the quality is the same as before. Maybe some things on the tactical side have changed. We can see some things in the video analysis.

"The other thing is the situation. It's the derby, it's a night game, it's live on TV. It's a lot more than Sheffield against Barnsley and I think that makes the game so different."

Stendel sees it as a no-lose situation for a club with no wins in their last nine League one games and one from bottom.

"The feeling against Leicester and Oxford (two draws), especially when you concede a red card (as they did early in both games), what you can expect against a top team in the league goes down from everybody and you say, 'Okay, we can only win.' The game has this feeling a little bit.

"But there's also a responsibility for Barnsley Football Club to know it is a Yorkshire derby. It's maybe the most important derby for this club.

"It can maybe help to bring energy. We can fight against them more and we can only win in this game."

As for special plans for DKD, "not a lot," he replies, "but it's clear he's a really good player in this league.

"A lot of players know his quality in front of the goal, especially in the box. We have to look after him.

"Wednesday has a lot of quality players but he's surely a player that we have to mark."

Kevin Blackwell staying on is the right call

#2010. Sheffield United vs Watford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:37

Aiming to break into the top eight of the Championship table on their return from the November international break, Sheffield United will welcome Watford to Bramall Lane on Saturday.

The hosts lost in their final game before the break but sit just two points outside of the playoff spots, while their visitors sit five points above the drop zone thanks to a win and a draw in their last two outings.

Sheffield United head back into Championship action after the international break on Saturday aiming to reignite their pursuit of the playoff places.

Aiming to kick on from a 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a return to the Premier League, the Blades experienced a mixed start to the season but looked to have turned a corner after the September and October break.

The Blades managed four wins and one draw in their first six games back from that break, scoring 11 goals and conceding six in those games, culminating in a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham, with Ben Brereton Diaz on the scoresheet, and a 3-2 away victory against Preston North End thanks to Sydie Peck's hat-trick.

They were unable to carry that winning streak into the latest break, though, visiting Charlton Athletic last time out and losing 2-1, having fallen behind and levelled through Jordan Ayew before Matt Godden scored the winner for their hosts 10 minutes from time.

Now sat 10th but just two points behind seventh and eighth spots, Sheffield United will again hope to come back firing and return to winning ways at Bramall Lane on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to South Yorkshire aiming to build on a positive turn in form before the break.

After a 16th-placed Championship finish in 2025-26 and the summer appointment of Alessio Dionisi, Watford endured a poor start to the new campaign, picking up just 11 points from their first 13 matches, winning three and losing eight of those.

The Hornets' away record is a real cause for concern, having lost six and drawn one of their seven league matches on the road, scoring just four goals in those and conceding 14.

The most recent of those was a 3-2 away loss against Norwich City, in which they led 2-0 at the break, but Dionisi's men did bounce back, beating Lincoln City 1-0 at home thanks to Stephy Mavididi's goal, before they hosted then-leaders Middlesbrough last time out and stood strong for a point from a 0-0 draw.

Watford now return to action hoping to add to those positive results and extend their five-point lead over the relegation zone.

Sheffield Wednesday are unable to call on defender Femi Seriki, who sustained a long-term injury before the break, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One and Joe Rothwell may also remain sidelined.

Patrick Bamford may be in line for a return, though, having been out with a shoulder injury, and if deemed fit he could return up front from the start despite competition for those places from Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Jordan Ayew and Tyrese Campbell.

Kalvin Phillips has impressed in his second loan spell with the Blades thus far and will again join Sydie Peck in midfield.

Watford are still without Kwadwo Baah, Jeremy Ngakia, Soumaila Coulibaly and Edoardo Bove on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Kevin Keben and Branimir Mlacic should again join Mattie Pollock in the middle of the defence after their clean sheet against Middlesbrough last time out, while Krepin Diatta may start in a wing-back role if he is fit after being forced off in that game.

Competition for attacking spots is rife with Mamadou Doumbia, Amin Nabizada, Stephy Mavididi, Luca Kjerrumgaard, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma all pushing to start, while Myron Boadu has often led the line but missed the Middlesbrough game.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Donovan, Peck, Phillips, Brereton Diaz; Cannon, Bamford

#2007. Why the moral lessons of Scottish lower league football really are important – Craig Levein

We often take pride in Scotland in our more authentic, less corrupted professional football. Sure, it lacks the glitz and glamour of the English game, awash with American and Middle Eastern money, but as a result it has remained more rooted in our communities, and more accessible to the working class fans who made the game great in the first place.

The recent Man City scandal has only served to sharpen this contrast. While Pep Guardiola’s teams played undeniably beautiful football, the subsequent revelations of financial impropriety have put the validity of their titles under question and damaged the sporting credibility of the Premier League.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has shone a light on the trade-offs English football has had to make: creating an elite, globally renowned product, but at the cost of affording dubious characters free rein over long-standing, treasured community institutions.

READ MORE: Scotland's most beautiful football ground is such a pastoral delight that even Subbuteo noticed

Scotland’s approach has been different. There is less money, to be sure, but that has insulated the Scottish game from some of this scandal. As a result, it feels more real, a purer form of the game.

However, the truth is that Scottish football is a tough place to ply your trade. This is especially true in the lower divisions, where I started my career with Cowdenbeath in the early 1980s.

Football at this level couldn’t feel further removed from the clashes between Wall Street billionaires and petrostates so common south of the border. It was hard work and often brutal. Although we might take pride in it, the undeniable truth is that for many clubs further down the pyramid, life is tough. Razor thin margins, poor facilities, and low attendances can make it demanding work both on and off the pitch.

It’s hardly surprising then, contrary to how we might see ourselves, that Scottish clubs are not immune to finding themselves reliant on financial benefactors whose interest in them, and in the areas they represent, is passing. When the money dries up, the very existence of these clubs comes under threat.

Take Gretna FC as an example. In 2008, two years after appearing in the Scottish Cup Final, and enjoying a sustained run in the top-flight for the first time in their history, the club was forced into liquidation. Gretna’s owner, Brooks Mileson, who died later that year, was posthumously declared bankrupt.

This tragic episode shows the dangers of overreliance on financiers who promise big and briefly deliver, before things come crashing down; a similar fate very nearly befell Dumbarton FC in 2024, when the club went into administration and were only saved by a takeover at the last minute. When the worst happens, there is little that loyal, matchgoing fans can do other than pick up the pieces and start again.

Responsible stewardship then, in the cutthroat world of the Scottish lower divisions, is worth more than silverware. One standout example of this is my friend, Kevin Mackie, chairman of Brechin City. Since 2021, Kevin has done an incredible job stabilising the fan-owned club after a turbulent few years which saw successive relegations consign them outside the SPFL for the first time in 67 years.

Things are finally looking up; last season, the Hedgemen only narrowly missed out on promotion back into League Two. As I write, they sit third in the Lowland League and are among the favourites to challenge this season.

This is encouraging progress under Kevin’s astute leadership. It shouldn’t come as a surprise given his extensive experience as a local businessman, running successful car dealerships in the Brechin area for several decades, as well as hotels and commercial properties.

Kevin also understands what Gretna and Dumbarton seemingly didn’t: that reliance on distant financiers is fraught with danger, and that the loyalty that defines the relationship between fan and club is seldom present in the corporate world.

Kevin’s car dealership closed almost overnight when his suppliers; Renault, Nissan, and Dacia, along with their banking subsidiary RCI Bank (now Mobilize Financial Services) terminated supply and financing agreements for unclear reasons. It’s a demonstration that the dangers of financial reliance we see so often in football permeate through many other industries – though there are important differences.

Kevin has launched a legal claim in search of answers and closure, but five years on a resolution remains frustratingly elusive. This is what shocks me as a football professional. As a manager, I had to face the press immediately after each game and defend my actions. A string of bad results could easily see me fired.

In business, and in law, this sort of direct accountability can be hard to find. The wheels turn slowly and the process is often very opaque. Troublingly, this culture is now seeping into football, as the lengthy legalistic wrangling over Man City shows. In Scotland, we may not be immune from this.

Despite these difficulties, Kevin can take inspiration from the Brechin fans who stood by their club throughout some tough years. Dedication and loyal support define football, but business can be a different beast. Although football resembles business more and more each day, with Man City showing the ugliest side of this, we shouldn’t lose sight of what makes the game beautiful, especially north of the border.

Business and the law could learn a lot from what makes football so special, and so popular worldwide. As a dedicated steward of his local team, leading them back from some tough times, Kevin represents that as well as anyone.

Craig Levein is a former Hearts player, Scotland international and manager

#2003. Leyton Orient vs AFC Wimbledon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 23:48, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:22

AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.

The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.

Leyton Orient head into the weekend in 14th spot in the League One table after recording five wins, two draws and six defeats in their 13 league games this term.

Orient cruised to a 3-0 victory in their most recent league outing against Cambridge United at the end of October, a result that has formed part of a three-game winning run on home turf.

Their last victory at Brisbane Road took place in the FA Cup first round, which saw Idris El Mizouni net a brace in an emphatic 5-1 win over sixth-tier Harborough Town to set up a second-round tie against Port Vale.

However, Richie Wellens's side were unable to repeat that sort of success in their away clash against Barnet in the EFL Trophy, falling to a 4-2 defeat as they finished at the bottom of Group F and behind third-place Wimbledon on goal difference.

Orient will now return to the familiar surroundings of Brisbane Road, where they have won four of their last five outings, including three victories without conceding in their previous four home league games.

That represents a significant improvement from the start of the season when they lost each of their opening three home matches in the third tier.

Wimbledon have played a game more than Orient, but they are a point worse off after winning four, drawing four and losing six of their 14 League One matches.

In fact, the Dons have lost four of their previous six games in the third tier, although they did manage to end an 11-game winless run in all competitions in their most recent outing against Blackpool.

Alistair Smith's first-half proved enough to fire Wimbledon to a 1-0 victory, representing their first three-point haul since recording back-to-back wins against Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in September.

After enjoying success at Plough Lane, Johnnie Jackson's side will now make the trip to Brisbane Road for the second time this season after playing out a 1-1 draw in August's EFL Trophy encounter.

They missed out on a bonus point with a defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout, but they enjoyed greater success in January's league visit, when they fought back from a goal down to claim a 3-1 victory.

However, their hopes of repeating that success may be tempered by the fact they have lost six of their last eight competitive away games, including each of their last four.

Orient midfielder Ollie O’Neill will be out for around four months after undergoing an operation not long after returning from a long injury absence.

The hosts are also expected to be without the services of Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare.

Rarmani Edmonds-Green will feature alongside Alfie Gilchrist in central defence after returning from injury to start the wins over Cambridge and Harborough.

As for the visitors, Wimbledon are unable to call upon Josef Bursik, Dan Sweeney, Dujuan Richards, Ryan Johnson and Donnell McNeilly due to injury.

Jayden Stockley will serve a one-match ban after being sent off for two bookable offences in the narrow win over Blackpool.

Aaron Sasu could move forward to replace Stockley in the frontline, which would open the door for Steven Sessegnon to feature at left wing-back.

Baxter; Stevens, Edmonds-Green, Gilchrist, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, Wellens, Dobra; Kabia

Bishop; Tilley, Yiadom, Ogundere, Seddon, Sessegnon; Smith, Harrison, Maycock; Cornick, Sasu

Leyton Orient have made Brisbane Road a fortress in recent times, and considering Wimbledon have lost five of their seven away league games this season, we think the signs point to a home win on Saturday.

#2001. Mario Frick savours Aberdeen ‘paradise’ as heavy metal football takes precedence over cynical rave murmurings

Although he rates it as one of his best football memories, Mario Frick learned a painful lesson after scoring against Scotland at Hampden 16 years ago.

He injured himself in the resulting melee with his Liechtenstein teammates and had to be substituted. “They gave me an injection but it didn't help,” he recalled. "In the seventh minute of stoppage time we lost 2-1 - which is football. It was my last year in international football, maybe my last goal for the international team at around 36-years-old.”

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was a reminder of the perils of over celebrating. The cynic might say the new Aberdeen manager has come to the right place. The Pittodrie side haven’t scored for three matches and have recorded the fewest shots on target in the league this season.

There doesn’t seem much danger of him erupting with joy and bumping his head on the roof of those tight Pittodrie dugouts. Albeit, he will have to wait for the chance to take a bow at the stadium having replaced the sacked Stephen Robinson during the international window. Trips to Rugby Park and then Ibrox await before he can enjoy the comforts of home for the first time against Dundee at the end of this month.

Although there was no game on at Pittodrie on Thursday, Frick's face adorned the jumbo screen in the corner as he was officially welcomed to the club ahead of being “formally unveiled”, as the club described it. Even the empty stadium, he said, gives him “goosebumps”. He regards it as a temple. Nowhere is the reverential air more intoxicating than in the Sir Alex Ferguson Lounge, where Frick was presented to reporters for the first time. “Pure football,” he said, while gazing at the photographs adorning the walls.

The Aberdeen training facility at Cormack Park is better than anything he encountered in Switzerland, where he played and managed. “It is paradise,” he said. He’s clearly keen to linger awhile, to which the reply might be: Good luck with that. While he occupies a unique position as the first Liechtenstein player to become a professional footballer, Frick is slightly less exceptional when it comes to Aberdeen.

The 52-year-old is the 27th permanent manager at Pittodrie, stretching back to 1903. That averages out at about one every four-and-a-half years, which isn’t too bad. However, as many as 16 have come and gone since Ferguson left for Old Trafford 40 years ago this month. The recent anniversary celebrations – Manchester United being the ones celebrating rather than Aberdeen, who have rued the day almost ever since – were a reminder of the significance of that November’s morning in 1986, when it was announced he was heading south.

No club is immune to the difficulties of trying to replace a successful manager, as Manchester United have spent the last 13 years proving. Aberdeen have not been completely feckless without Fergie. A Scottish Cup here, a League Cup there. They haven’t been relegated either. Not yet at least.

Steering the side away from danger is Frick’s first task, starting this weekend against the only team currently below them: Kilmarnock. He knows what’s involved having taken over at his previous club, Luzern, five years ago when they were deep in relegation trouble. They parted company this summer.

“They were bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points when I took over there and the whole environment was similar to now,” he said. “We saved them and progressed from there. I am sure I can do the same now at Aberdeen. I am very ambitious and now it is important to get out of this situation and we want to go to the top six.”

The noises coming out of Pittodrie in recent days is that Frick likes to play ‘front foot, attacking football’, which seems to mirror the promises made by every new manager these days. Isn’t that what Sebastien Pocognoli trumpeted when he was unveiled as Scotland manager three months ago? The alarm bells might be growing louder for Aberdeen fans. Frick explained his “heavy metal football” philosophy. “It is high pressing, it is counter pressing, it is vertical play and creating many goalscoring chances,” he said. “That is heavy metal.”

Supporters will argue that anything’s better than what a team coached by Frick’s predecessor was producing. Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington referred to the new manager's “warm personality” and suggested local journalists should look forward to getting to know the new man. Frick is an urbane character though one it might be advisable to avoid crossing. Trim and sporting a military haircut, he doesn’t look as if he will accept having his authority challenged.

As for the vexed question of the captaincy, with Kevin Nisbet giving the impression that the responsibility weighs heavily on him, Frick confirmed the striker will retain the armband against Kilmarnock. “Afterwards, I will have to decide what we do,” he said.

Frick speaks five languages with various levels of proficiency. His German and Italian are perfect. “English I need to improve,” he said. “I started learning English in school but never used it.” He recently started English tuition online “with an Australian who lives in France” with a view to working at a British club. “My only ambition now is to bring success to Aberdeen,” he said.

The fans will hope that such a zeal for self-improvement is catching. When Ferguson once ordered his players to have no fears about going to Glasgow and winning, now a sense of trepidation infects so much at the club. Aberdeen have just announced that a “Hacienda Classical” rave night event at Pittodrie on 28 May will no longer be going ahead. Someone queried online whether it was a case of the calendar needing to be left clear for relegation play-offs. Confidence is rock bottom.

Frick relishes the challenge. “I am ready!” he said. “I have had a five-month holiday! I am full of energy.”

#1999. Home James! Stone and Waters are back at Saffrons

The pair, who played influential roles in Town's Southern Combination League play-off triumph, return to Jude Macdonald's squad following spells away from the club.

Stone's return adds proven firepower to Town's attacking options, with the forward having scored 20 goals in 47 appearances during the 2024/25 campaign. His goalscoring exploits helped Town establish themselves back in the Isthmian League South East Division following a ten-year absence, as Macdonald's side enjoyed an impressive first season back at Step 4.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Stone is also closing in on a personal milestone, having made 91 appearances for the club, leaving him just nine short of a century in a Town shirt.

Meanwhile, Waters' return sees Macdonald reunited with a player who has been central to his tenure at The Saffrons. The midfielder holds the distinction of being Macdonald's first signing following his appointment as manager in the summer of 2022, going on to become a regular fixture in the side over the following seasons.

Waters made 123 appearances and scored 23 goals during his first spell with Town, playing an important role in the club's rise from the Southern Combination Premier Division to the Isthmian League.

He departed for Haywards Heath Town earlier this summer but now returns to The Saffrons, renewing his association with the manager under whom he enjoyed considerable success.

Both players featured in the Town squad that secured promotion through the play-offs in May 2024, ending the club's decade-long absence from the Isthmian League. Stone scored Town's second goal in the final.

Their return brings valuable experience of Macdonald's playing style and the demands of Step 4 football, as Town look to improve their position in the South East Division after a tough start.

For Stone, the move offers a chance to rediscover the goalscoring form that made him one of Town's most effective attacking players and return to his boyhood club, while Waters will look to resume the most promising spell of his career at the club.

Town are at home to Whitstable on Saturday.

#1998. Motherwell plan to shock Rangers at Fir Park as Ibrox lessons taken into ‘electric’ battle

Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson says the Steelmen will take key lessons from their Ibrox battle with Rangers into Saturday night’s rematch at Fir Park.

The 8pm kick-off live on Sky Sports is set to bring an added edge to proceedings with those in claret and amber improving after six straight Premiership losses. They are unbeaten in their last three games while Rangers failed to win in North Lanarkshire last season, drawing under Russell Martin and then Danny Rohl.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Now it’s current manager Derek McInnes’ turn to try and mastermind an away win at Motherwell, but last time out in Govan, the away side dominated the ball with almost 60% possession. Rangers still created several chances though during the 1-0 win with manager Johansson keen to see a focused approach this weekend.

He said: “We know we are a good team and we can do good stuff. That was good, but we don’t use our positive play to score goals. That is something we are working hard on and know we have to improve.

“We want to create more and we are. We are in the top five in the league for chances created and so on. We are on the right path there. In the last game against Rangers, I also learned that you have to take care of defensive transitions against teams like that. This is a fantastic challenge against a good side.

“We are also in a moment of progression and we have some continuity in the team. We feel like we can compete and we are looking forward to the game. They are good in second-ball play and in transitions. We need to be a good version of ourselves if we are going to get points. There has to be a focus on how we attack and defend.”

Johansson added: “It will be a big occasion and I am looking forward to it a lot. The guys have been fantastic in training and we love to play these games. I came to Motherwell for many reasons, but these fixtures were part of it. To play here on a Saturday evening when it’s dark outside the lights go on is fantastic.

“There will be a lot of people in the stands and it’s going to be electric. It will be much better than playing the bounce game here last week when there was nobody in the stadium. It’s a big difference to that! I see the progression of my team and development leads to results. We are moving in the way we want to do things.”
